title: Your First Weekend at Dartmouth College, Shared as Cards
description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Kick Off Your Arrival
cards.subtitle: Orientation Check-In at Mass Row
cards.notes: Start your journey by picking up your Dartmouth ID and room keys at the check-in tents. House Community leaders will be there to welcome you to your new home.
cards.short_summary: The official starting point for new students to receive IDs and housing keys.
cards.evidence_claim: Orientation Check-In, ID and Key Pick-Up, and House Community Welcome for students occurs at Massachusetts Row during assigned times.
cards.source_title: Arrival and Move-in - New Student Orientation - Dartmouth
cards.access_notes: Check-in typically runs from 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. on scheduled arrival days.

cards.title: Bond with Your 'Trippees'
cards.subtitle: Outdoor Orientation Tradition
cards.notes: Join a student-led group for hiking, organic farming, or nature writing. It is a cornerstone tradition for meeting classmates before fall term classes begin.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing student-run outdoor orientation program for incoming freshmen.
cards.evidence_claim: First-Year Trips are a student-run orientation program run by the Dartmouth Outing Club since 1935, offering activities like climbing and organic farming.
cards.access_notes: Participation is optional but highly encouraged for all incoming first-year students.

cards.title: Refuel at 'FoCo'
cards.subtitle: The Main Campus Dining Hall
cards.notes: Grab a meal at the various stations, from the omelet bar to Ma Thayer's. It is the social hub for first-year students on the Ivy Unlimited meal plan.
cards.short_summary: The primary all-you-care-to-eat dining facility on the Dartmouth campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Class of 1953 Commons, known as FoCo, features multiple food stations including a vegan station and Ma Thayer's for daily selections.
cards.source_title: What I Eat in a Day at Dartmouth!
cards.access_notes: Open daily for breakfast, lunch, and dinner; requires a meal plan swipe or payment.

cards.title: Explore the Stacks
cards.subtitle: Academic Heart of Campus
cards.notes: Visit the Orozco murals and find your favorite study nook. The library is a central hub for research, advising, and late-night academic sessions.
cards.short_summary: The main library complex at Dartmouth, home to significant murals and study spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Baker-Berry Library is a hub for learning at the center of campus, offering academic resources and the famous Orozco murals.
cards.access_notes: Open daily; Berry Library typically stays open until 12:00 a.m. for students.

cards.title: Get Inspired by Art
cards.subtitle: Free Campus Art Museum
cards.notes: Walk through the galleries to see global collections. Admission is always free, making it an easy spot to visit with new friends between orientation sessions.
cards.short_summary: A teaching museum with a diverse collection of art from around the world.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission to the Hood Museum of Art is always free for everyone, and it offers student-led tours and events.

cards.title: Late Night Fun
cards.subtitle: Weekend Student Activities
cards.notes: Head to the Collis Center for late-night food, concerts, and comedy. These events provide a safe, alcohol-free social environment every Friday and Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A student-led program providing late-night entertainment and social events.
cards.evidence_claim: Collis After Dark offers late-night social and entertainment events every Friday and Saturday, including concerts and food.
cards.source_title: Collis After Dark | Collis Center for Student Involvement
cards.access_notes: Events typically take place late on Friday and Saturday nights.

cards.title: Walk the River Trails
cards.subtitle: Nature Escape Near Campus
cards.notes: Take a break from the bustle of orientation with a walk along the Connecticut River. The trails are easily accessible from the north end of campus.
cards.short_summary: A 100-acre forested park with trails adjacent to the Dartmouth campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Pine Park features over 100 acres of forested land and trails parallel to the Connecticut River, popular for student walks.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from dawn to dusk for foot travel.

cards.title: Touch History
cards.subtitle: Rare Books and Archives
cards.notes: Visit Webster Hall to see rare manuscripts and the college archives. It's a quiet, brightly-lit space where you can get hands-on with primary sources.
cards.short_summary: The home of Dartmouth's rare books, manuscripts, and college archives.
cards.evidence_claim: Rauner Special Collections Library houses over 100,000 rare books and the Dartmouth College Archives in Webster Hall.

cards.title: Sunday Morning Tradition
cards.subtitle: Classic Hanover Diner
cards.notes: Enjoy a hearty breakfast or a famous baked good at this Main Street staple. It's a favorite spot for students to gather and recap their first weekend.
cards.short_summary: An iconic Hanover diner and bakery serving the Dartmouth community since 1947.
cards.evidence_claim: Lou's Restaurant & Bakery is a cornerstone of the Dartmouth experience, known for its breakfast and the 'Lou's Challenge' tradition.
cards.source_title: Cafés in Hanover: Part 7 (Lou's Bakery) - Dartmouth Admissions
cards.access_notes: Opens early at 6:30 a.m. daily; popular for breakfast and brunch.

cards.title: Find Your Community
cards.subtitle: Club and Organization Fair
cards.notes: Browse hundreds of student organizations on the Green. This is the best time to sign up for clubs, from a cappella groups to the outing club.
cards.short_summary: An annual fair where students can learn about and join campus organizations.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Involvement Fair is held before classes begin, allowing students to learn about hundreds of clubs and organizations.
cards.source_title: Orientation | Collis Center for Student Involvement
cards.access_notes: Typically held on the Green the day before fall term classes begin.
